title: Laser-Driven Electron Stripping from Nanoparticles in Plasma
abstract: Laser wakefield accelerators use plasma wake waves to produce high-energy electron beams over short distances. Nanoparticles can trigger localized electron injection, with their size and density influencing the accelerated beam charge. However, the electron charge of a nanoparticle does not determine how much charge is stripped by the laser. Here we show that a quasistatic electrostatic model predicts laser-driven electron stripping from nanoparticles, in agreement with particle-in-cell simulations in vacuum and helium plasma. The model identifies a saturation density that increases with laser amplitude and decreases with nanoparticle radius, separating complete from partial stripping. Above this density, the stripped electron fraction decreases and the stripped charge approaches a finite limit. Multicycle pulses produce more stripped charge than the model predicts due to time-dependent electron dynamics. In helium plasma, plasma wake waves induce additional electron stripping. These results give an understanding of the scaling of laser-driven electron stripping from nanoparticles and could inform nanoparticle parameter selection for future nanoparticle-assisted laser wakefield accelerators.
